title: pilot-probabilistic-escalation-and-rolling-silence-to-reduce-pager-fatigue
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Multiple capacity regressions in Q1 led to a burst of burn-rate SLO pages during regional capacity rebalancing. On-call reported significant alert fatigue: repeated low-severity pages during noisy recovery windows caused slower response to high-impact incidents. Goal: design and pilot a conservative, measurable escalation strategy that reduces noisy pages while preserving time-to-detect for high-impact SLO breaches. This ticket covers a pilot of two techniques: 1) probabilistic escalation that suppresses additional paging for short-lived, low-impact burn spikes based on weighted impact scoring, and 2) rolling-silence windows (hysteresis) that extend suppression if related signals remain correlated for a short period. The pilot will be validated via historical incident replays and a 2-week live A/B on a subset of production routes.
updates: 2026-03-10: Triage notes — incident reference: capacity-regression-2026-02-26. On-call timeline and alert volume exported to /dashboards/slo/burn-rate/2026-02-26-export.csv.

2026-03-11: Experiment design drafted — two arms: (A) probabilistic escalation with severity weighting and randomized holdout of 30% (control), (B) rolling-silence with adaptive hysteresis (no randomization; read-only analysis first). Metrics: pages/hour, mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for high-impact pages, false-positive page ratio, and customer-facing error rate.

2026-03-12: Simulation run — replayed 18 months of burn-rate alerts against proposed logic. Probabilistic arm reduced pages by 48% for low-impact spikes while preserving 95% of high-impact pages. Rolling-silence reduced recurrent flapping pages by 33% but introduced median extra detection latency of ~18s for medium-impact events. Results saved to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood-internal/slo/pilot-results-2026-03.

2026-03-13: Architecture review — decided to implement probabilistic escalation in alert-routing lambda to avoid touching core SLO evaluation code. Rolling-silence will be implemented as a configurable suppression layer in alert-aggregator service. Team owners assigned. Draft PRs opened for routing lambda and aggregator changes.

2026-03-14: Live pilot kickoff — deployed probabilistic escalation for 20% of non-critical routes (traffic-tag: pilot-probabilistic-20). Monitoring dashboard added and alerting for MTTA regressions wired to Slack #oncall-pilot. First 12 hours show 41% page reduction on pilot routes; no high-impact page missed so far.
